characters.name: The Petrie Family
characters.description: Actor Allusion: In the 2004 reunion, Rob has become a computer enthusiast who makes his own animations for fun, just like Dick Van Dyke. Author Avatar: Rob Petrie is based on Carl Reiner, who actually played the part himself in the unaired pilot. Much of Rob's background — his army experience, his courtship of his wife, and his life in the suburbs — is taken directly from Reiner's life. Several episodes also came from Reiner's life, including obscure topics such as picking up the check when with friends. Character Tics: Laura Petrie had a habit of weeping with a histrionic, incoherent warble ("Ooohhh, Rooooob~!") whenever she suffered enough stress, based off an example Carl Reiner gave Mary Tyler Moore. Closely resembling the iconic whimpering ofStan Laurel, it became something of a minorSignature Move, as she went on to use it in other shows. Clingy Jealous Girl: Laura dislikes any hint that another woman might be making a move on Rob, as shown by a number of episodes like "The Foul Weather Girl", "The Man from Emperor" and of course, "Jealousy". During at least one episode, she threatened to "quietly kill" a girl Rob used to know if she decided to flirt with her husband and Rob describes her usual response to being jealous as sitting there with aSlasher Smile. Crazy Jealous Guy: One of the few ways to get the ordinarily friendly, patient Rob riled up is to hit on Laura. Tracy Rattigan found this out the hard way when when Robfood slappedhim multiple times for doing so.

characters.name: The Helper Family
characters.description: Catchphrase: Millie often says, "What are you talking about? What's he talking about? What are you talking about?" with no pause in between. She occasionally inserts other activities in place of "talking about". The Ditz: Millie is prone to coming up with ill-thought-through plans. It's All About Me:Played for Laughs; when Jerry is hypnotized into acting like his hero, he acts like himself. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Jerry is egotistical, insensitive, and prone to sometimes-cruel practical jokes, but is ultimately a very loyal friend and husband. Replacement Flat Character: The writers avoided making Laura a typical ditzy sitcom housewife by letting her best friend, Millie, be the ditzy one who comes up with most of the zany schemes.

characters.name: The Alan Brady ShowStaff
characters.description: Honorary Aunt: She appoints herself Richie's aunt immediately after seeing him and Rob and Laura, who are both friends with her, don't mind at all. Introverted Cat Person: More like Lonely Cat Person; Sally is a brash woman, but she's also single and unhappy about it. At least one episode had her talking to her cat, Mr. Henderson, about how neither of them had anywhere to go that evening. One of the Boys: Sally, which was exemplified in "Sally is a Girl" with various jokes such as explaining that a poker game won't have any women; just Rob, Buddy and Sally. Sarcastic Devotee: Rob and Buddy aren't immune to Sally's wit, but she's very fond of both of them and has been known to involve herself in some pretty big things to help them or make them happy. All Jews Are Cheapskates: Zigzagged; Buddy (who is explicitly Jewish) always had "a guy" to get anything at a good deal. However, he is emphatically shown many times to be a very generous guy (and his "deals" are meant to help his friends).
